title: Test Pyramid Builder — Spend a Testing Budget
description: A budget simulator for test strategy: drag or tap bundles of unit, component, integration, API, end-to-end and manual tests onto a building site and watch the shape you build get named (pyramid, ice-cream cone, testing trophy, hourglass). A live model estimates suite runtime, flake exposure, monthly maintenance and confidence per risk area, with plain-language insights about where your hours are going.
prompt: Build me a 'Test Pyramid Builder'. I want to drag or tap bundles of unit, component, integration, API, E2E and manual tests into a pyramid, with a fixed authoring-hours budget that you can't overspend. Next to it, a live model should show suite runtime, flake exposure, maintenance cost and confidence, with confidence broken down by risk area so an all-unit suite visibly has blind spots. Add presets for the healthy pyramid, the ice-cream cone anti-pattern, the testing trophy and an hourglass, and explain each one. The shape label should come from the proportions I actually build, not from whichever preset I clicked. Make the model's assumptions explicit and clearly labelled as illustrative. Warm, architectural look — sand and terracotta, bricks, not another dark dashboard.

methodology: Formula oracle: for a hand-built suite (2 unit bundles + 1 E2E bundle) the spec asserts runtime and flake exposure against values computed by hand from the documented model (302 s / 4 workers; 1 − ∏(1 − p)^n).
Metamorphic comparison: the ice-cream cone must be slower, flakier and more expensive to maintain than the healthy pyramid, whatever the exact constants are.
Classifier table test: each preset is loaded and its computed shape name and explanation are checked, proving the label comes from the proportions and not from the button.
Boundary checks on the budget: filling to the limit, attempting one more add, the disabled + control and the over-budget message.
Input-mode coverage: tap-to-add on both projects, and a real mouse drag (plus a drag released off-target) on desktop.
Visual review at 1280px and 390px for brick rows staying centred and labels legible on every brick colour.
risks: The drag gesture double-adding: a drag ends with pointerup and a click on the same button, so the click must be suppressed.
Shape classification rules overlapping (a trophy-like build also satisfying the hourglass rule) so the label flips unexpectedly.
State restored from localStorage leaking into tests, which is why the spec loads the page with ?fresh.
qa.playwright: Everything the model computes is rendered as DOM text with data-testid hooks, so assertions are plain toHaveText and numeric comparisons rather than reading gauge widths. The drag used page.mouse down/move/up with steps, because pointer capture needs intermediate pointermove events to cross the drag threshold; locator.dragTo also works but hides the off-target case. On the Pixel 7 project the drag test is skipped with test.skip(isMobile, ...) and the tap path covers touch users. The brick drop animation is disabled via emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }), and no screenshots are compared because the value is in the numbers, not the pixels.
coverage: All four presets classified and explained
Tap-to-add, remove, and exact runtime/flake formula values
Budget limit, over-budget message, disabled add control, clear
Mouse drag onto the site and drag released off-target (desktop)

a11y: Every bundle is a real button that adds on click or Enter, and each pyramid layer has labelled + and − buttons, so dragging is never required. The shape name, explanation, insights and budget messages are aria-live, and every gauge has its value as text beside it.
